the-wagner-story-book-firelight-tales-of: William Henry Frost retells the stories of Wagner's great operas — the Ring, Lohengrin, Tannhäuser, and more — as fireside tales for young readers. Gods, heroes, dragons, and doomed love unfold in prose versions of the mighty music dramas. A wonderful first doorway into Wagner for children not yet ready for the opera house.
schwatka-s-search-sledging-in-the-arctic: William Henry Gilder accompanied Lieutenant Frederick Schwatka's 1878 expedition into the Arctic, sledging hundreds of miles in search of records from Sir John Franklin's lost expedition. His account of cold, hunger, and endurance among the Inuit is a classic of polar literature. A gripping true story of one of the great searches of the age.
the-duenna-a-comic-opera: Sheridan's sparkling comic opera — with music by his father-in-law Thomas Linley — weaves mistaken identities and young love through a Spanish setting. Its wit and melody made it one of the great hits of the London stage. Readers can enjoy the libretto's verbal fireworks even without the music.
voyages-of-peter-esprit-radisson-being-a: Pierre Radisson — the daredevil coureur de bois — recounts his incredible travels among the Indigenous peoples of the Great Lakes in the 1600s. Captured, adopted, escaped: his adventures read like fiction but helped open the fur trade. One of the most thrilling true narratives of early Canada.
history-of-the-ottawa-and-chippewa-india: Andrew J. Blackbird — himself an Ottawa chief's son — wrote this history of the Ottawa and Chippewa Indians of Michigan, adding a grammar of their language and his own reminiscences. A rare nineteenth-century Indigenous voice telling its people's story in its own terms. Invaluable for historians and deeply moving for any reader.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abdera: This 1913 reference piece on Abdera, the Thracian city of Democritus and Protagoras. Laughing philosophers came from its walls. The entry notes its coins and ruins. An old Greek town, remembered for its wise men. Its air was said to breed dull wits and sharp tongues.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abraham-a-san: This 1913 reference article on Abraham a Sancta Clara — the witty Augustinian preacher of old Vienna. Nikolaus Scheid celebrates his humor and fire. His sermons mixed jokes with judgment. Austria's beloved pulpit voice. His Judas the Arch-Rogue made all Vienna laugh.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abraham-ben-m: A 1913 entry on Abraham ibn Ezra — the wandering Jewish scholar, poet, and Bible critic. Anthony Maas honors his restless genius. Spain, Italy, and England all knew his staff. A medieval mind of the first rank. His Bible notes still puzzle and delight scholars.
